Where a lapse traces to the compilation procedure - an unassigned compiler, a missing source record - raise the correction against the procedure in the same review. Attach the confirmation with its counts and actions.

evidenceHint.en: Register confirmation for the period: rows due, rows submitted, rows lapsed with their reasons, and the corrections raised

text.en: Filter the register to rows whose due date has passed.
Match each row to a submitted report or a recorded reason.
Count the rows submitted on time, late and not at all.
Raise a correction for every lapse traced to the procedure.

title.en: Record the management body accountable for cybersecurity and what each of its roles answers for

description.en: Name the body that carries cybersecurity accountability for this entity rather than leaving it assumed. Record which body that is - board, executive committee or the equivalent - list the roles that sit on it, and against each role state what it answers for in relation to cybersecurity: approving the measures, overseeing their implementation, or receiving the reporting. Record where this is written down (terms of reference, delegation of authority, governance manual) so the accountability survives a change of individuals. Attach the governance record with the date it was adopted.

evidenceHint.en: Governance record naming the management body, its roles, what each answers for in cybersecurity, and the document the accountability is written into

text.en: Name the body that approves the cybersecurity measures for this entity.
List the roles sitting on it and what each answers for.
Cite the terms of reference or delegation that records this.
Record the date the governance record was adopted.

title.en: Approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures at the management body and minute the resolution

description.en: Put the set of risk-management measures in force to the management body as a decision item rather than an information item, with enough detail for the body to know what it is approving: the measures, the risks they address, and what remains unaddressed. Minute the resolution naming the version of the measures approved, the date, and the members present. That minute is the artifact an auditor asks for when testing whether the body approved the measures, so record it as a resolution with its own reference rather than as a line inside general minutes.

evidenceHint.en: Board cybersecurity resolution: the version of the measures approved, the date, the members present, and its own minute reference

title.en: Schedule the management body's cybersecurity oversight reviews and define the pack presented at each

description.en: Fix the cadence at which the body will review cybersecurity, and write down what it will be shown each time, so oversight is a standing item rather than something that only follows an incident. Record the agreed interval, the standing agenda, and the contents of the pack - movement in the risk register, the status of the approved measures, open incidents and those reported to the authority, and the actions outstanding from the last review. Record who prepares the pack and how long before the meeting it is issued. Attach the terms of reference or standing agenda carrying both.

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference or standing agenda stating the oversight cadence, the pack contents, who prepares it and when it is issued

text.en: Agree the interval between cybersecurity oversight reviews.
List the items the pack must carry at every review.
Name who prepares the pack and when it is issued.
Add the standing item to the body's forward agenda.

title.en: Log each management body cybersecurity review with the decisions taken and their owners

description.en: After every scheduled review, record what the body was shown, what it decided, and who owns each action with the date it is due. File the pack that was presented alongside the minute, because a minute on its own does not evidence what the body actually saw. Where the body accepted a risk or deferred a measure, record that explicitly as a decision with its rationale - a deferral that appears nowhere is indistinguishable from an oversight failure when it is examined later.

evidenceHint.en: Management oversight log for the period: date, pack presented, decisions taken, and actions with owners and due dates

text.en: File the pack presented alongside the minute of the review.
Record each decision the body took, with its rationale.
Assign an owner and a due date to every action raised.
Carry open actions forward into the next review's pack.

title.en: Verify the cybersecurity measures in force still match the set the management body approved

description.en: Compare the measures actually operating against the version the body approved in its resolution, and list every difference: measures added since, measures dropped, and measures whose scope has changed. For each difference say whether it needs the body's approval or falls within a delegation already recorded. Take the differences that need approval back to the body as a decision item rather than noting them in a report, and record the outcome against the resolution. Attach the comparison with its date and the version of the measures it was made against.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of the measures in force against the approved version, listing each difference and whether it was taken back to the body

title.en: Register the management members required to complete cybersecurity training and their current status

description.en: List the people, not the seats. One row per member of the management body, carrying the role, the date they joined it, whether they have completed cybersecurity training, the date they last completed it, and the syllabus version they were taught. Take the membership from the governance record that names the body, so the roster and the accountability record cannot drift apart, and refresh it whenever the body's membership changes. Attach the roster export with the date it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Management training roster: member, role, date joined the body, training completed, date last completed and syllabus version

title.en: Define the cybersecurity training syllabus for the management body and the material it is taught from

description.en: Decide what the training will actually cover and write it down, so the training records point at something specific rather than at an attendance line. Build the syllabus from the organisation's own material rather than a generic course: the risks its risk assessment identified, the measures the body approves and oversees, the incident reporting obligations and their timelines, and the accountability the body carries. State the delivery method, the duration, and the provider or internal presenter. Version the syllabus, because the roster records which version each member was taught. Attach the syllabus and its material.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned management cybersecurity training syllabus with its material, stating the topics covered, the delivery method, duration and presenter

text.en: Draw the risk topics from the organisation's own risk assessment.
Cover the measures the management body approves and oversees.
Include the incident reporting obligations and their timelines.
State the delivery method, the duration and who presents it.
Version the syllabus so the roster can cite which one was taught.

title.en: Add cybersecurity training to the induction of newly appointed management members

description.en: A roster that is complete today goes stale at the next appointment, so put the training into the induction rather than into a reminder. Amend the induction checklist used when someone joins the management body to include the cybersecurity syllabus, name who arranges the session, and state the point in the induction by which it is expected. Agree the change with HR, who issue and file the induction checklist, and confirm the amended version is the one actually in use rather than leaving the old one in circulation. Attach the amended checklist with its version and effective date.

evidenceHint.en: Amended management induction checklist showing the cybersecurity training item, who arranges it and when it is expected, with its version and effective date

title.en: Collect the completed-training record for each management member, with its date and syllabus version

description.en: As each member completes the training, file the evidence and update their row on the roster: the date completed, the syllabus version taught, the delivery method, and the attendance or completion record from the presenter or the training platform. Where a member attended only part of a session, record what they covered rather than marking the row complete. The roster and these records together are what an auditor reads as the management training records, so keep them in one place with the roster.

evidenceHint.en: Management training records: per member, the completion or attendance evidence with the date completed and the syllabus version taught

text.en: File the attendance or completion evidence per member.
Record the date completed and the syllabus version taught.
Update that member's row on the training roster.
Record partial attendance rather than marking a row complete.

title.en: Identify the management members with no completed training and report the gaps to the body

description.en: Read the roster against the current membership of the management body and list every member with no completed training, or whose training was against a syllabus version since superseded. Put that list, with the reason for each gap, into the pack for the body's next oversight review rather than into a mailbox, so the body sees its own coverage. Record the date each outstanding member is booked to complete the training. Attach the gap list with the review it was reported to.

evidenceHint.en: Training gap list for the period: members with no completed training or a superseded syllabus version, the reason, the booked date, and the review it was reported to
